method: S1 is the open RACGP AJGP 2022 LARC review, fetched and checked verbatim (29 claims, 6 of them doses). A1 is AMH, read under subscription and PARAPHRASED across the 'Contraception' and 'Emergency contraception' topics (47 claims, 18 doses); no passage reproduced, no source_text stored. THE SOURCES CONFLICT ON IUD DURATION and the OPEN one is the out-of-date one: S1 (2022) says both hormonal IUDs are licensed for up to five years, while A1 (July 2026) gives the levonorgestrel IUD as 5 OR 8 years. Both are stated with their dates and the guideline says plainly which is current. This is the reverse of the usual pattern in this corpus and is flagged because a reader who trusts the quotable source over the unquotable one would be wrong here. Failure rates and device figures are flagged dose:true because they are the numbers a patient decides on.

claims.claim: Long-acting reversible contraceptives including hormonal and copper intrauterine devices and the contraceptive implant provide highly effective set-and-forget contraception suitable for provision in general practice, have very few contraindications and can be recommended as first-line options across the reproductive lifespan from adolescence to perimenopause
claims.source_text: LARCs, including hormonal and copper-bearing intrauterine devices (IUDs) and the contraceptive implant, provide highly effective 'set-and-forget' contraception, which are suitable for provision in general practice. 3 They have very few contraindications and can be recommended as first-line contraceptive options across the reproductive lifespan, from adolescence to perimenopause.

claims.claim: PBS claims for hormonal IUDs and implants almost doubled between 2006 and 2018, Medicare data indicate a more than three-fold increase in IUD insertion procedures for people aged 15 to 24 years in the past 10 years, and a recent survey estimated 10.8% of women aged 15 to 44 years were using a LARC
claims.source_text: In Australia, uptake of LARCs has been increasing, with Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) claims for hormonal IUDs and implants almost doubling between 2006 and 2018, and Medicare Benefits Schedule data indicating a more than three-fold increase in IUD insertion procedures for people aged 15-24 years in the past 10 years. 6,7 A recent survey also estimated that 10.8% of women aged 15-44 years were using a LARC.

claims.claim: The Australian Contraceptive ChOice pRoject showed that a combination of training doctors in providing LARC information and rapid access to LARC insertion clinics increases LARC uptake
claims.source_text: The recently completed Australian Contraceptive ChOice pRoject showed that a combination of training doctors in providing LARC information and rapid access to LARC insertion clinics increases LARC uptake.

claims.claim: Copper IUDs are effective immediately after insertion, are not PBS-listed and generally cost 70 to 100 dollars, last 5 to 10 years depending on the type, and might make menstrual bleeding heavier and more prolonged which can limit their use for some patients
claims.source_text: Copper IUDs are effective immediately after insertion. 12 Copper IUDs are not PBS-listed, generally costing $70-$100. They last 5-10 years, depending on the type. They might make menstrual bleeding heavier and more prolonged, which can limit their use for some patients.

claims.claim: A copper IUD can be used as post-coital emergency contraception when inserted within five days of unprotected sexual intercourse after excluding risk of an earlier established pregnancy, and if all episodes of intercourse in the cycle were in the past five days it can be inserted regardless of where in the cycle
claims.source_text: Copper IUDs can be used as post-coital emergency contraception when inserted within five days of unprotected sexual intercourse and after excluding risk of an earlier established pregnancy. 15 If all episodes of intercourse in the cycle were in the past five days, the copper IUD can be inserted regardless of when it is in the cycle.

claims.claim: If unprotected intercourse occurred earlier than five days before copper IUD insertion, conservative advice is that it should be inserted by day 12 of the cycle to ensure insertion occurs before implantation of an early pregnancy
claims.source_text: If unprotected intercourse occurred earlier than five days prior to copper IUD insertion, to ensure insertion of the copper IUD occurs before implantation of an early pregnancy, conservative advice is that it should be inserted by day 12 of the cycle.

claims.claim: Hormonal IUDs are only immediately effective if inserted between days one and five of the menstrual cycle, otherwise they require seven days to become effective
claims.source_text: In contrast, hormonal IUDs are only immediately effective if inserted between days one and five of the menstrual cycle, otherwise they require seven days to become effective.

claims.claim: S1 states that the insertion technique is identical for the 19.5 mg and 52 mg levonorgestrel IUDs and that both are licensed for up to five years of use
claims.source_text: The insertion technique is identical for both devices, and both are licensed for up to five years of use.

claims.claim: The 19.5 mg levonorgestrel IUD insertion might be easier and associated with less discomfort given the smaller insertion tube and device dimensions, so it could suit people with a relatively small cervical canal or uterine cavity including nulliparous and younger people
claims.source_text: Kyleena insertion might be easier and associated with less discomfort than Mirena, given the smaller insertion tube and device dimensions. 18 As a result, Kyleena could be a suitable option for people with a relatively small cervical canal and/or uterine cavity, including nulliparous and younger people.

claims.claim: Because of its lower hormone dose the 19.5 mg levonorgestrel IUD is not licensed for management of heavy menstrual bleeding or for endometrial protection with menopausal hormone therapy, and is not recommended for extended use from the age of 45 years
claims.source_text: As a result of its lower hormone dose, Kyleena, unlike Mirena, is not licensed either for the management of heavy menstrual bleeding or for endometrial protection with menopause hormone therapy (MHT) and is not recommended for extended use from the age of 45 years.

claims.claim: S1 gives effectiveness as 99.7% for the 19.5 mg levonorgestrel IUD and 99.9% for the 52 mg levonorgestrel IUD, with serum levonorgestrel levels at 90 days of about 140 and about 280 ng per litre respectively
claims.source_text: Effectiveness 99.7% 33 99.9% 34 … Serum LNG levels at 90 days 35 ~140 ng/L ~280 ng/L

claims.claim: S1 gives device dimensions of 28 by 30 mm with a 3.8 mm insertion tube for the 19.5 mg levonorgestrel IUD, against 32 by 32 mm with a 4.4 mm insertion tube for the 52 mg device
claims.source_text: Device dimensions (width × height, mm) 28 mm × 30 mm 32 mm × 32 mm Insertion tube 3.8 mm 4.4 mm

claims.claim: S1 gives amenorrhoea rates of 12.3% at 1 year and 23% at 5 years for the 19.5 mg levonorgestrel IUD, against 18.6% at 1 year and 30 to 40% at 5 years for the 52 mg device
claims.source_text: 12.3% at 1 year 23% at 5 years 18.6% at 1 year 30-40% at 5 years

claims.claim: S1 states that with both IUDs there can be increased bleeding and spotting days in the first 6 months of use, and that by 3 years of use most people have fewer than 4 bleeding or spotting days per month
claims.source_text: There can be increased bleeding and spotting days in the first 6 months of use with both IUDs. By 3 years of use, most people have fewer than 4 bleeding or spotting days/month.

claims.claim: In a study the proportion of people with no period pain rose from 50% at baseline to 80% in users of both IUDs at 3 years
claims.source_text: In a study, the baseline number of people with no period pain at the start of the study was 50%. This improved to 80% in users of both IUDs at 3 years

claims.claim: If pregnancy occurs with a hormonal IUD about half of those pregnancies will be ectopic, however because IUDs are so effective at preventing pregnancy IUD users are less likely to have an ectopic pregnancy while they have an IUD than when they do not
claims.source_text: If pregnancy occurs with a hormonal IUD, about half of those pregnancies will be ectopic (outside the uterus). 33,34 However, because IUDs are so effective at preventing pregnancy, IUD users are less likely to have an ectopic pregnancy while they have an IUD than when they do not have an IUD

claims.claim: S1 states that expert opinion supports extended off-label contraceptive use of the 52 mg levonorgestrel IUD if inserted aged 45 or more and of copper IUDs if inserted aged 40 or more, in both cases until menopause or age 55, while extended use of the 19.5 mg device is not recommended
claims.source_text: Extended use not recommended If inserted aged ≥45 years, can be used for contraception until menopause or aged 55 years 12 If inserted aged ≥40 years, can be used for contraception until menopause or aged 55 years

claims.claim: Menopause is a clinical diagnosis after which contraception is no longer required, diagnosed after 12 months of amenorrhoea after turning 50 years of age, or following 24 months amenorrhoea in those aged below 50
claims.source_text: Menopause is a clinical diagnosis, after which time contraception is no longer required. For people not using hormonal contraception, it is diagnosed after 12 months of amenorrhoea after turning 50 years of age, or following 24 months amenorrhoea in those aged below 50 years.

claims.claim: For patients using a levonorgestrel IUD, implant or progestogen-only pill who have been amenorrhoeic at least 12 months since turning 50, a single serum FSH level can determine the need for ongoing contraception: if FSH is above 30 IU per litre contraception is only required for one more year, and if 30 or below contraception is still required and FSH can be rechecked in a further year
claims.source_text: For patients using an LNG IUD, contraceptive implant or progestogen-only pills who have been amenorrhoeic for at least 12 months since turning 50, updated guidance recommends that a single-serum follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) level can be used to determine the need for ongoing contraception. If FSH is >30 IU/L, contraception is only required for one more year. If FSH is ≤30 IU/L, contraception is still required, and the FSH can be rechecked in a further year if required.

claims.claim: When the 52 mg levonorgestrel IUD is used to protect the endometrium as part of a menopausal hormone therapy regimen it should be replaced at five years and extended use beyond five years for this indication is not advised, and no other progestogen-only contraceptive is licensed for endometrial protection
claims.source_text: It should be noted that when Mirena is used to protect the endometrium as part of an MHT regimen, it should be replaced at five years. Extended use beyond five years for this indication is not advised. No other progestogen-only contraceptives are licensed for endometrial protection and cannot be used as part of an MHT regimen.

claims.claim: For patients using a menstrual cup with an IUD, advice should be given on how to check IUD threads after menses and how to gently release the suction before cup removal to avoid the threads getting caught between the cup and vaginal wall
claims.source_text: For patients using a menstrual cup with an IUD, provide advice on how to check their IUD threads after menses and how to gently release the suction before cup removal to avoid the threads getting caught between the cup and vaginal wall.

claims.claim: Patients should be encouraged to attend for review if IUD threads cannot be felt or there is concern the IUD has moved, with medical review including speculum examination, urine pregnancy test and pelvic ultrasound with or without X-ray if threads are not visible
claims.source_text: General practitioners (GPs) should encourage patients to attend for review if the IUD threads cannot be felt or there is concern the IUD has moved. Medical review includes a speculum examination to look for visible IUD threads, a urine pregnancy test to exclude pregnancy and pelvic ultrasound +/- X-ray if threads are not visible.

claims.claim: The etonogestrel single-rod contraceptive implant provides 99.95% effective contraception for up to three years, and there is no need to replace it earlier than three yearly for overweight or obese individuals due to lack of evidence of increased pregnancy risk
claims.source_text: The etonogestrel single-rod contraceptive implant provides highly effective (99.95%) contraception for up to three years. 5 There is no need to replace the implant earlier than three yearly for overweight/obese individuals due to lack of evidence of increased pregnancy risk.

claims.claim: Troublesome bleeding is the most common side effect leading to discontinuation of the implant, with one in five users having amenorrhoea, three in five infrequent irregular bleeding and one in five frequent or prolonged bleeding, and approximately half of those with frequent prolonged bleeding will improve after three months
claims.source_text: Troublesome bleeding is the most common side effect leading to discontinuation of the implant. It is helpful to explain the range of expected vaginal bleeding, which is: one in five users have amenorrhoea; three in five users have infrequent, irregular bleeding; and one in five users have frequent or prolonged bleeding. Approximately half of those with frequent prolonged bleeding will improve after three months.

claims.claim: Recommended implant insertion has been updated following case reports of nerve injuries or intravascular insertion, informed by a cadaver study finding no major neurovascular structures 8 to 10 cm proximal to the medial epicondyle and 3 to 5 cm posterior to the sulcus, with the Australian product information updated in January 2020
claims.source_text: Recently, there have been updates to the recommended insertion site following a small number of case reports of nerve injuries or intravascular insertion. 29 The new recommended site for insertion was informed by a study of 40 female cadaver arms, in which no major neurovascular structures were identified in the area 8-10 cm proximal to the medial epicondyle and 3-5 cm posterior to the sulcus, suggesting this window is theoretically safer than other areas of the arm. … The Australian product information for Implanon NXT was updated to reflect these findings in January 2020.

claims.claim: S1 gives the implant insertion site as 8 to 10 cm proximal to the medial epicondyle and 3 to 5 cm posterior to the bicipital groove in the non-dominant arm with the arm flexed at the elbow and hand underneath the head, inserted subdermally over the triceps muscle, and if it is not possible to insert 3 to 5 cm from the sulcus it should be inserted as far from the sulcus as practical
claims.source_text: Patient positioning: The patient's arm should be flexed at the elbow with the hand underneath the head (or as close as possible). - Insertion site: 8-10 cm proximal to the medial epicondyle and 3-5 cm posterior to the bicipital groove (this is the sulcus between biceps and triceps muscles) in the non-dominant arm. This means that the implant will be inserted subdermally (superficially) under the skin, over the triceps muscle. Measure and mark the insertion site. If it is not possible to insert the implant 3-5 cm from the sulcus (eg a person with thin arms), it should be inserted as far from the sulcus as practical.

claims.claim: It is important not to attempt removal of impalpable implants, and instead to consider a pregnancy test and additional contraception, check the previous insertion site and arm, arrange local imaging and removal under ultrasonography guidance if possible, and if the implant cannot be found in the arm consider chest X-ray as rare events of migration to the pulmonary vessels have been reported
claims.source_text: It is important not to attempt removal of impalpable implants. Consider pregnancy test and additional contraception (if required), check the previous insertion site (and arm), arrange local imaging (X-ray and/or ultrasonography) and removal under ultrasonography guidance, if possible. If the implant cannot be found in the arm, consider chest X-ray, as rare events of migration to the pulmonary vessels have been reported.

claims.claim: Superficial insertion remains crucial to safe implant technique, with the needle visible throughout and the skin lifted or tented while the needle is inserted horizontally into the subdermal plane, and before removal the implant should be checked to be palpable and superficial
claims.source_text: Superficial insertion remains crucial to safe insertion technique. It is important to be able to visualise the needle throughout the insertion procedure and to lift or 'tent' the skin while the needle is being inserted in the horizontal direction into the subdermal plane. 32 Before attempting implant removals, always check that the implant is palpable and superficial.

claims.claim: It continues to be recommended that only professionals who have undergone training perform implant procedures, and IUD training includes theoretical learning and supervised insertions in a clinical setting available through state or territory family planning organisations, some IUD-inserting GP educators, gynaecologists and hospitals
claims.source_text: It continues to be recommended that only professionals who have undergone training perform implant procedures. … IUD training includes theoretical learning and supervised insertions in a clinical setting and is available through state or territory family planning organisations, some IUD-inserting GP educators, gynaecologists and hospitals.
